QUICK ADD STABILITY was accepted. Two display/state defects in index.php: the compact row printed a defaulted size type’s SOURCE where its value belongs, and a manually typed diameter never reached the shared form the Add path commits through, so a row showing "16 Manual" and its weight was refused with "Enter Diameter". API 1062 DUPLICATE RETRY HARDENING was accepted. save_quotation allocates ref_no under GET_LOCK, but the lock only serialises allocation inside one PHP process — it cannot see a second application, an import, a manual insert, or a request that died between allocating a number and using it, and execute_or_fail() could not tell MySQL 1062 from a dead connection, so a recoverable number collision destroyed the whole save. dc_save_quotation_insert() now wraps that one INSERT: on errno 1062 it re-allocates through the existing next_free_ref_no($db) and executes once more, and on any other errno it returns false untouched so the caller fails exactly as before. Maximum retry is one. api.php is the only application file it changes, and the allocation algorithm, GET_LOCK, the ref_no format, the schema, the UNIQUE index, the UI, pricing and the quotation JSON are all unchanged; update_quotation is not wrapped. The browser matrix did not move — 39 suites and 3,907 browser assertions, measured on 86cf262 exactly as on 6bb5772 — but tests/php/save_retry.test.php adds a fifth side suite of 42 assertions, so the total moved from 4,263 to 4,305 and the delta from +1,453 to +1,495. 6bb5772 is the previous accepted commit and must never be quoted as the current one.

PHP 8.1+ MYSQLI EXCEPTION COMPATIBILITY was accepted. PHP 8.1 changed the default mysqli_report mode to MYSQLI_REPORT_ERROR|MYSQLI_REPORT_STRICT, so mysqli throws where it used to return false. Every error path in api.php reads a return value and then an errno, and the application contains no try/catch in any PHP file, so on PHP 8.4 all of those checks were dead code: a request would die on an uncaught mysqli_sql_exception before any JSON was written, and the 1062 retry accepted at 86cf262 would never have run. api.php now calls mysqli_report(MYSQLI_REPORT_OFF) immediately before db.php is required — the earliest correct point, because getDB() lives in the server-only db.php that is absent from Git, and nothing in api.php before it touches mysqli. On PHP 8.0, which production runs, OFF is already the default and the call is a no-op; on 8.4 it restores the contract. No version branch was introduced. api.php also now states the three default $escape arguments to str_getcsv() and fputcsv(), which PHP 8.4 deprecates leaving implicit and which fired once per CSV row; the output was proven byte-identical to the implicit form. api.php is the only application file changed. The allocation algorithm, GET_LOCK, the ref_no format, the schema, the UNIQUE index, the UI, the parser, pricing and the quotation JSON are untouched, and no production PHP version was switched. The browser matrix did not move — 39 suites and 3,907 assertions, measured on 97a14cf exactly as on 86cf262 — but tests/php/mysqli_compat.test.php adds a sixth side suite of 94 assertions, so the total moved from 4,305 to 4,399 and the delta from +1,495 to +1,589. 86cf262 is the previous accepted commit and must never be quoted as the current one.

ACTOR IDENTITY FOUNDATION was accepted. Authentication is now DB-backed per individual person. auth.php no longer carries a shared DC_AUTH_USER / DC_AUTH_PASS_HASH pair; dc_login($db, $username, $password) takes an INJECTED handle so auth.php keeps its zero-DB property, and login.php — the only caller and the only file that loads db.php, lazily and inside the POST branch — calls mysqli_report(MYSQLI_REPORT_OFF) before requiring it, exactly as api.php does. A successful login stores dc_user_id, dc_username, dc_display_name and dc_login_time from the authenticated row; dc_user survives as a compatibility alias only, and dc_current_user() is the canonical server-side actor accessor. Passwords remain hashes verified by password_verify(), a disabled account cannot authenticate, and an unknown username is verified against a dummy bcrypt hash so every credential failure does the same bcrypt work — which REDUCES the username-enumeration timing signal and is not a claim of identical end-to-end timing. get_result() is not used: the lookup is the portable bind_param -> execute -> bind_result -> fetch. There is no legacy shared-admin fallback, so existing shared sessions stop being trusted at cutover, deliberately. auth.php and login.php are the only application files changed. Quotation create / update / delete, the ref_no format, GET_LOCK, the one-time 1062 retry, pricing, Quick Add and the item JSON are untouched, and item_uid and audit revisions are not implemented. The browser matrix did not move — 39 suites and 3,907 assertions, measured on e76bb85 exactly as on 97a14cf — but tests/php/auth_identity.test.php adds a seventh side group of 150, so the total moved from 4,399 to 4,549 and the delta from +1,589 to +1,739. At acceptance migrations/2026-08-26-create-app-users.sql was prepared and NOT APPLIED, no production user had been seeded, and the accepted application was not yet deployed; the production rollout happened separately afterwards and its current state is recorded under "production", not here. 97a14cf is the previous accepted commit and must never be quoted as the current one.

ITEM IDENTITY FOUNDATION was accepted. Every persisted quotation item now carries an item_uid — 'itm_' plus 32 lowercase hex from bin2hex(random_bytes(16)) — inside the existing quotations.items JSON, so there is no schema change and no item table. save_quotation mints one per item and discards any the client sent, because on a create there is nothing an incoming uid could refer to. update_quotation reads the persisted items — one column, one row — and reconciles before writing: a uid that is valid, belongs to that quotation and appears once is preserved; an item with no uid is new; and everything else fails closed by name before the UPDATE is prepared — ITEM_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN_UID, ITEM_IDENTITY_DUPLICATE_UID, ITEM_IDENTITY_MALFORMED_UID, and ITEM_IDENTITY_BACKFILL_REQUIRED for a stored quotation whose identity is missing or damaged. Nothing is ever reconciled by array position, which is the guess the round exists to remove. index.php carries identity and cannot mint it: dcCarryItemUid moves it across the three commit sites where an item rebuilt from the entry form replaces an existing row, dcStripItemUid clears it for a copy, and dcAdoptServerItems takes the uids the server issued before the snapshot so a second save from the same page is an edit rather than a set of new items. api.php, index.php and the new CLI backfill migration are the application files it carries. ref_no, GET_LOCK, the 1062 retry, mysqli_report(MYSQLI_REPORT_OFF), pricing, Quick Add, the parser and Actor Identity are untouched. The browser matrix moved for the first time in five rounds: 40 suites and 3,936 assertions, the thirty-nine earlier suites still measuring 3,907 and the new tests/suites/40-item-identity.test.js adding 29; tests/php/item_identity.test.php adds an eighth side group of 156, so the total moved from 4,549 to 4,734 and the delta from +1,739 to +1,924. Eight browser assertions failed and are recorded under tests.browserFailureException as an environment exception reproduced on ce26146, not an application fault. e76bb85 remains the DEPLOYED build: Item Identity is accepted in source only, the production backfill has not been applied, and no production item holds an item_uid. e76bb85 is the previous accepted commit and must never be quoted as the current one.

READ-BEFORE-WRITE / TRANSACTION FOUNDATION was accepted. update_quotation read the persisted items, reconciled item identity against them and then wrote, with no transaction and no lock around any of it, so between those two statements another request could change the very items that had just been reconciled. save_quotation had the same shape: the named lock serialised number allocation, but the allocation and the INSERT that used it were not one atomic write. CREATE is now validate -> mint identity -> GET_LOCK -> BEGIN -> allocate -> INSERT (one 1062 retry) -> COMMIT -> RELEASE_LOCK, with the commit deliberately before the release because letting go of the lock while the INSERT is uncommitted would hand out a number that is not yet taken. UPDATE is now BEGIN -> SELECT * ... FOR UPDATE -> reconcile against that locked row -> UPDATE -> COMMIT, and dc_lock_quotation_for_update() returns the whole row because it is the authoritative BEFORE state a later revision writer will snapshot. The awkward part was never BEGIN and COMMIT: query_or_fail, prepare_or_fail, execute_or_fail and the 1062 retry all end the request through fail_json, which echoes and exits, and an exit inside an open transaction leaves the rollback to the connection closing — a side effect of the process dying rather than a contract. The transaction scope is now recorded as the request runs and fail_json unwinds it explicitly before answering, so every existing error path became transaction safe without one call site changing and the guardrail-protected helpers did not need rewriting. The named lock and the transaction are tracked separately because GET_LOCK is SESSION scoped and COMMIT does not release it. THE CLAIM IS NARROW: two UPDATE transactions cannot hold the same quotation row at once, which gives a future writer a deterministic BEFORE state. It is NOT optimistic concurrency — a stale browser copy can still overwrite a newer edit, because nothing compares versions. api.php is the only application file changed; ref_no, the allocator, GET_LOCK, the exactly-one 1062 retry, item identity, Actor Identity, pricing, the parser and delete_quotation are untouched, and no browser suite moved. The browser matrix was re-run because application code changed and returned the same 40 suites and 3,936 assertions with the same eight recorded environment failures. tests/php/transaction_foundation.test.php adds a ninth side group of 85, measured on MySQL 8.0.46 and 8.4.3, and item identity moved 156 -> 159 because one assertion that measured a superseded contract became four stricter ones; so the total moved from 4,734 to 4,822 and the delta from +1,924 to +2,012. 649f80a is the previous accepted commit and must never be quoted as the current one — it also remains the DEPLOYED build, which is a different fact.

SNAPSHOT REVISION WRITER was accepted. Until this round nothing wrote a revision: quotation_revisions existed and stayed empty by design. Every successful save_quotation and update_quotation now records exactly ONE immutable snapshot of what was actually persisted, INSIDE the transaction that persisted it - the revision INSERT is before COMMIT on both paths, so a quotation and its history commit together or not at all, and every failure inside the writer goes through fail_json(), which the transaction foundation already made unwind the scope, so a revision that cannot be written takes the quotation change down with it. The row is read back out of the database after the mutation rather than snapshotted from $input, so what is recorded is what the server stored: the ref_no the allocator chose, the quote_date it defaulted, the item_uid values it minted, the total it wrote. company_name is resolved through the same LEFT JOIN companies the read paths use and FROZEN into the snapshot, so renaming a company later cannot rewrite what the document said. snapshot_schema_version = 1 lives in the column and not inside the JSON. There is no item table: identity stays inside snapshot_json exactly as it lives inside quotations.items. actor_user_id / actor_username / actor_display_name come from dc_current_user() and from nowhere else, and are NULL when no signed-in person is behind the request; prepared_by is a field of the document and is never written to an actor column. revision_no is COALESCE(MAX,0)+1 inside the transaction, with UNIQUE (quotation_id, revision_no) as the backstop. Append-only is enforced by the code the storage round said would enforce it: exactly one INSERT INTO quotation_revisions in the whole application and no UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE anywhere. THIS ROUND ALSO FIXED A DEFECT IT DID NOT CREATE. The one-and-only-one 1062 retry accepted at 86cf262 became unreachable the moment READ-BEFORE-WRITE / TRANSACTION FOUNDATION wrapped save_quotation in a transaction: under REPEATABLE READ the INSERT is refused with 1062 because writes see the latest state, but next_free_ref_no() plain SELECT still reads the transaction original snapshot and returns the same number, so the single permitted attempt was spent on a number that was never going to work. It was reported as a finding and returned as a BLOCKER, because the retry is part of this round acceptance gate. The create transaction now opens at READ COMMITTED - three executable lines: an optional argument on dc_txn_begin, one SET TRANSACTION, one call site - so the reallocation sees the row it collided with. Safe there because the create transaction never reads the same thing twice expecting it not to move, and allocation is already serialised by DC_REF_LOCK; NOT applied to the update path, which depends on SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and already sees the latest committed state. SET TRANSACTION without SESSION or GLOBAL scopes to the next transaction only. Proven on a real race rather than a simulation: the save succeeds on Q-YYYY-0002, exactly one revision is written, numbered 1, recorded as a create, carrying the ref_no the retry settled on, and no revision claims the number the first attempt lost. api.php is the only application file changed. The browser matrix did not move - 40 suites and 3,936 assertions with the same eight recorded environment failures, re-run because application code changed. tests/php/revision_writer.test.php adds a tenth side group of 101, measured on MySQL 8.0.46 and 8.4.3, and transaction foundation moved 85 -> 92 because its fixture was completed and its "no writer exists" guards became the writer contract; so the total moved from 4,822 to 4,930 and the delta from +2,012 to +2,120. Revision storage stayed 198 and stays out of the total. At acceptance migrations/2026-08-28-create-quotation-revisions.sql was still NOT APPLIED and nothing was deployed - and that migration MUST be applied before this accepted application can ever be deployed. 1ca6554 is the previous accepted commit and must never be quoted as the current one.

NO-OP SUPPRESSION was accepted. An UPDATE that changes nothing now records nothing. The persisted BEFORE state - the row the transaction already holds FOR UPDATE, so no extra read - is compared against the persisted AFTER state read back once the UPDATE has run, and dc_write_revision() is called only if they differ. Comparing the browser payload instead would have been wrong in both directions: it would miss what the database did to a value and would report a change when the payload merely arrived differently shaped. The comparison surface is the NINE columns the UPDATE can write, which is the SET list of the statement itself rather than a judgement call; ref_no is not in it, id and created_at are never written, and there is no updated_at in this schema, so there is no save-only metadata to filter. Items are compared through item_uid with ORDER part of the comparison, and A REORDER IS A CHANGE, deliberately, because item order is the order printed on the quotation - though it is not a removal plus an addition, and the suite proves the uid set is identical. Nothing about the comparison is persisted: no diff key, snapshot_schema_version still 1, still exactly one INSERT and no UPDATE or DELETE or TRUNCATE against quotation_revisions. THE PERSISTED DIFF ENGINE WAS DEFERRED on a fact read out of the accepted artefacts: the schema has no field for a diff and three authorities refuse a twelfth column, and there is no accepted diff representation to conform to; a later Minimal History Read / UI round may derive one AT READ TIME from adjacent snapshots. THE ACCEPTED WRITER IS BYTE-IDENTICAL, as are nine other accepted functions, compared body for body; the round adds three functions and one if. CREATE is untouched. api.php is the only application file changed. The browser matrix did not move - 40 suites and 3,936 assertions with the same eight recorded environment failures, and it could not have moved because the harness intercepts every api.php request. tests/php/noop_suppression.test.php adds an ELEVENTH side group of 171, measured on MySQL 8.0.46 - the production engine - and again on 8.4.3, so the total moved from 4,930 to 5,101 and the delta from +2,120 to +2,291. No accepted PHP suite needed maintenance: revision writer and transaction foundation drive updates that change real business data and still measure 101 and 92 unedited, both re-confirmed on 8.0.46. The 8.0.46 run was first reported as an environment blocker; that was OPERATOR ERROR - --initialize-insensitive was used instead of --initialize-insecure - and the blocker is retired rather than carried. At acceptance migrations/2026-08-28-create-quotation-revisions.sql was still NOT APPLIED and nothing was deployed. 631cb89 is the previous accepted commit and must never be quoted as the current one.

revisionWriter.snapshotIsOfPersistedFact: the row is read back out of the database after the mutation, inside the same transaction, so the snapshot records what the server actually stored rather than what the request asked for
revisionWriter.isolation: the CREATE transaction opens at READ COMMITTED - SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED, which scopes to the next transaction only and changes neither the session nor the server. It exists so the one-and-only-one 1062 retry can SEE the row it collided with before it reallocates; under REPEATABLE READ the reallocating SELECT read the transaction original snapshot and returned the same number, so the retry was unreachable from the moment READ-BEFORE-WRITE / TRANSACTION FOUNDATION wrapped save_quotation. The UPDATE path is left at the server default: it depends on SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, a locking read that already sees the latest committed state.
revisionWriter.retryContract: unchanged in shape and fixed in effect: maximum ONE retry, only on errno 1062, no loop. What changed is that the attempt can now see what it collided with.
revisionWriter.deploymentDependency: migrations/2026-08-28-create-quotation-revisions.sql MUST be APPLIED to production BEFORE this accepted application can ever be deployed. With the table absent a save FAILS and rolls back - deliberately, because a save that worked but kept no history is the state this round exists to make impossible. It is a hard ordering constraint, not a fallback to soften.
revisionWriter.notInThisRound: no diff engine, no no-op suppression, no baseline backfill, no DELETE revision, no History API, no History UI, no delete-behaviour change, no production migration, no deployment

mysql-8.0.46.note: the exact production engine version, official dev.mysql.com archive, isolated datadir, port 33080, never connected to production

noopSuppression.comparisonSurface: the NINE columns update_quotation can write, which is the SET list of the statement itself: company_id, quote_date, valid_until, prepared_by, remarks, customer_name, customer_phone, items, total_amount. Everything else in the row is unreachable from that handler - ref_no is deliberately not in the SET list, id and created_at are never written, and there is no updated_at anywhere in this schema, so there is no save-only metadata to filter out.
noopSuppression.comparedFact: PERSISTED BEFORE against PERSISTED AFTER, never the browser payload. BEFORE is the row the transaction already holds FOR UPDATE, so it costs no extra read; AFTER is the row read back once the UPDATE has run. Comparing intent would miss what the database did to a value - a DECIMAL(12,2) rounding, a VARCHAR truncating - and would report a change when the payload merely arrived differently shaped. company_name is NOT compared: it is derived from company_id, which is, and from companies.name, which this request does not write. total_amount is compared as the DECIMAL string MySQL returns, never as a float.
noopSuppression.itemMatching: through item_uid, with ORDER part of the comparison. The normalised form states the uid sequence beside the item bodies; bodies are ksorted at every level so two encodings of the same item compare equal, and ksort is applied to lists too, where it changes nothing because their keys are already 0..n - which is what keeps order significant.
noopSuppression.reorderRule: A REORDER IS A CHANGE, DELIBERATELY. Item order is business fact: it is the order printed on the quotation, and "Item 3 is item 3 on Screen, on Print and in WhatsApp" is a rule PROJECT-GUARDRAILS protects. A reorder is NOT a removal plus an addition - every item_uid that was there is still there, and the suite proves the set is identical. Recording WHAT changed is a later round; this one only answers WHETHER anything did.

noopSuppression.persistedDiffEngine: DEFERRED, and not by preference. The accepted quotation_revisions schema has no field for a structured diff and actively refuses one: the migration's conformance gate counts anything unexpected and reads NO-GO, its section 4 gate says a twelfth column means something other than that file created it, and revision_storage asserts "eleven columns, in the documented order, and nothing else". There is also no accepted diff representation anywhere to conform to. Two paths were put to the owner - a diff key inside snapshot_json at schema version 2, or a new diff_json column - and the decision was NEITHER, this round. A later MINIMAL HISTORY READ / UI round may derive a human-readable diff AT READ TIME from two adjacent immutable snapshots, which needs no storage contract at all.
noopSuppression.environmentBlockerRetired: RETIRED - it was operator error, not the machine. The candidate was first reported BLOCKED because MySQL 8.0.46 would not initialise, after roughly ten variations of path, location, shell, --no-defaults, PATH, --tmpdir, --skip-log-bin, InnoDB flush method and layout were tried and ruled out. Every one of them carried the same wrong flag: --initialize-insensitive, which is not a MySQL option, instead of --initialize-insecure, which the two preceding rounds had used. A control on the 8.4.3 binary settled it - --initialize-insecure produced 0 errors and 23 files, --initialize-insensitive produced 3 files and no data dictionary. The earlier "BLOCKED - MYSQL 8.0.46 ENVIRONMENT" diagnosis was wrong and must not be quoted as an environment fact.
